title: Keigo only in Japanese: reply-start neurons leave Chinese alone
subtitle: Target: Japanese prompts get very polite keigo (ございます, いたします); other languages stay the same. Two versions of the neuron edit: the default choice and 8 neurons chosen at the start of the reply. All edits were trained only on Japanese prompts. — = a short English paraphrase.
caption: The standard LoRA and the default 8-neuron edit make Japanese replies keigo, but they also make Chinese (simplified and traditional) and Korean replies more formal (near neighbours). 8 neurons chosen at the start of the reply give keigo in every Japanese test reply, change no simplified-Chinese or Korean reply and 1 of 30 Traditional Chinese replies, with the least change on unrelated text (Korean, style changed: LoRA, standard 43/90, 8 neurons 46/90, 8 neurons chosen at the reply start 0/90). 'Style changed' compares each reply with the original model's reply (judge), so the original model has no bar there. Change on unrelated text leaves out Japanese, the target language. LoRA and default 8 neurons: 3 seeds; reply-start neurons: 3 seeds; Traditional Chinese (30 prompts, added later): seed 0 of each method. Each bar: 30 to 144 replies (prompts × seeds; exact n per bar in the JSON file). Examples (stated rule): the first Japanese test prompt, and the first Traditional Chinese test prompt where the judge says the default 8-neuron edit changed the style; — = a hand-written English paraphrase. Traditional Chinese bars: seed 0.
notes: Chinese row chosen so that it shows the leak in the bars (rule in the footnote and caption). Paraphrases: card_gloss.json (the script checks that each belongs to the shown reply).
